def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic:
## Definition

Let $m\ge1$, let $G\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let
$f:G\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^3$ ([[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]];
the $C^3$ convention is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).
The one-dimensional conservation system with state domain $G$ is
$$u_t+\partial_x f(u)=0,\qquad u(t,x)\in G,$$
where $u$ is the conserved state and $f$ its flux. Its flux Jacobian is
$A(u)=Df(u)$. The system is **strictly hyperbolic on an open set $N\subseteq G$**
if, for every $u\in N$, $A(u)$ has $m$ distinct real eigenvalues, written in
increasing order $\lambda_1(u)<\cdots<\lambda_m(u)$. An **$i$th characteristic
family** on $N$ is a $C^2$ right-eigenvector field $r_i:N\to\mathbb R^m\setminus\{0\}$
with $A(u)r_i(u)=\lambda_i(u)r_i(u)$. It is **genuinely nonlinear** on $N$ if
$D\lambda_i(u)r_i(u)$ is nowhere zero there; after shrinking $N$ its sign is
constant. It is **linearly degenerate** on $N$ if $D\lambda_i(u)r_i(u)=0$
throughout $N$. Rescaling $r_i$ by a nonzero constant changes the wave-strength
parameter but not the family.

For $Q=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, a locally bounded map $u:Q\to G$ is a
**distributional weak solution with initial data $u_0$** if
$$\int_Q\bigl(u\cdot\varphi_t+f(u)\cdot\varphi_x\bigr)\,dt\,dx=0$$
for every vector test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Q;\mathbb R^m)$ and
$u(t,\cdot)\to u_0$ in $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^m)$ as
$t\downarrow0$. A **Riemann initial datum** is the step
$u_0(x)=u_L$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=u_R$ for $x>0$.
def-hll-two-wave-flux:
## Definition

For a two-state problem for a flux $f$ on the open state domain $G$ of
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]], choose explicit speeds
$S_L<S_R$. A signal speed means the propagation speed of one wave in the
particular Riemann solution being approximated. If the HLL model is used as an
enclosing approximation to that fan, its admissibility hypothesis is that
every such speed lies in $[S_L,S_R]$; this definition supplies no general
wave-speed bound.
Set $f_L=f(u_L)$ and $f_R=f(u_R)$. The HLL flux is
$$\widehat f_{\rm HLL}=\begin{cases}f_L,&0\le S_L,\\\dfrac{S_Rf_L-S_Lf_R+S_LS_R(u_R-u_L)}{S_R-S_L},&S_L<0<S_R,\\f_R,&S_R\le0.\end{cases}$$
In the middle case the model has three constant regions separated by the two
waves $S_L,S_R$ and one intermediate state. The wave-speed enclosure is a
separate hypothesis whenever an approximation claim uses it.
def-ideal-gas-euler-state-and-pressure:
## Definition

Fix $\gamma>1$. In one space dimension the conserved state is
$U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathbb R^3$, where $\rho$ is density, $m$ momentum, and
$E$ total energy per unit volume. The **admissible-state set** is the open set
$$\mathcal G_\gamma=\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\ E>m^2/(2\rho)\}.$$
The ideal-gas pressure on this set is
$$p(U)=(\gamma-1)\left(E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\right)>0,$$
the velocity is $u=m/\rho$, and the flux is
$$F(U)=\left(m,\frac{m^2}{\rho}+p,\frac{m}{\rho}(E+p)\right).$$
The sound speed is $c=\sqrt{\gamma p/\rho}$. These definitions apply only
on $\mathcal G_\gamma$; a state with nonpositive density or nonpositive
internal energy is inadmissible. The set is open because $\rho$ and
$E-m^2/(2\rho)$ are continuous on $\rho>0$ and the inequalities are strict;
all displayed flux functions are smooth on this domain.
def-rankine-hugoniot-and-lax-shocks:
## Definition

For a system as in [[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]], a
discontinuity with constant states $u_L,u_R\in G$ and speed $s\in\mathbb R$ is
a **Rankine–Hugoniot jump** if
$$f(u_R)-f(u_L)=s(u_R-u_L).$$
For a strictly hyperbolic system and $1\le i\le m$, it is a **strict Lax
$i$-shock** if it is a Rankine–Hugoniot jump and
$$\lambda_j(u_L)<s\ (j<i),\qquad \lambda_i(u_R)<s<\lambda_i(u_L),\qquad s<\lambda_j(u_R)\ (j>i).$$
An empty family of inequalities is omitted. A linearly-degenerate contact has
equal $i$-speeds on both sides, so it is not a strict Lax shock.
def-roe-linearization-and-flux:
## Definition

For states $u_L,u_R$ in the open state domain $G$ of
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]], a **Roe matrix** is a real matrix
$\widetilde A(u_L,u_R)$ such that
$$\widetilde A(u,u)=Df(u),\qquad \widetilde A(u_L,u_R)(u_R-u_L)=f(u_R)-f(u_L),$$
and $\widetilde A(u_L,u_R)$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb R$ with real
eigenvalues. If $\widetilde A=R\Lambda R^{-1}$, define
$|\widetilde A|=R|\Lambda|R^{-1}$ by replacing each diagonal eigenvalue with
its absolute value. The **Roe flux associated with this matrix** is
$$\widehat f_{\rm Roe}(u_L,u_R)=\tfrac12(f(u_L)+f(u_R))-\tfrac12|\widetilde A(u_L,u_R)|(u_R-u_L).$$
The jump identity is an algebraic conservation property. This definition does
not assert entropy admissibility of the approximate wave pattern.
def-scalar-convex-entropy-admissibility:
## Definition

For the scalar case of [[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]],
on $Q=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, a locally bounded function $u$ is a weak
solution of $u_t+f(u)_x=0$ if
$$\int_Q\bigl(u\,\varphi_t+f(u)\,\varphi_x\bigr)\,dt\,dx=0$$
for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Q)$. An **entropy pair** is a convex $C^2$
function $\eta$ and a $C^1$ flux $q$ satisfying $q'(u)=\eta'(u)f'(u)$. A weak
solution is **entropy-admissible for this pair** if
$\partial_t\eta(u)+\partial_xq(u)\le0$ in distributions; equivalently,
$$\int_Q\bigl(\eta(u)\,\varphi_t+q(u)\,\varphi_x\bigr)\,dt\,dx\ge0$$
for every nonnegative $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Q)$. For a single jump of speed
$s$, the entropy inequality requires
$q(u_R)-q(u_L)-s(\eta(u_R)-\eta(u_L))\le0$.
lem-smooth-simple-characteristic-eigenpa:
## Statement

Let $f:G\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^3$ and let $\bar u\in G$ be a state at which
$A(\bar u)=Df(\bar u)$ has distinct real eigenvalues
$\lambda_1^0<\cdots<\lambda_m^0$. For each $i$, there is a neighborhood $N_i$
of $\bar u$ and $C^2$ functions $\lambda_i:N_i\to\mathbb R$ and
$r_i:N_i\to\mathbb R^m$ such that $A(u)r_i(u)=\lambda_i(u)r_i(u)$,
$\lambda_i(\bar u)=\lambda_i^0$, and the eigenvectors can be normalized by a
fixed linear functional. After intersecting these finitely many neighborhoods,
the eigenvalues remain real, simple, and ordered, and $r_1(u),\ldots,r_m(u)$
form a basis at each $u$.
def-euler-star-pressure-response:
## Definition

Fix $\gamma>1$ and admissible left/right primitive states
$(\rho_K,u_K,p_K)$, $K\in\{L,R\}$, with $\rho_K,p_K>0$ and
$c_K=\sqrt{\gamma p_K/\rho_K}$. Set
$$A_K=\frac{2}{(\gamma+1)\rho_K},\qquad B_K=\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma+1}p_K.$$
For a trial star pressure $p>0$, the wave pressure response from side $K$ is
$$f_K(p)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{2c_K}{\gamma-1}\left[\left(\dfrac p{p_K}\right)^{(\gamma-1)/(2\gamma)}-1\right],&0<p\le p_K,\\(p-p_K)\sqrt{\dfrac{A_K}{p+B_K}},&p\ge p_K.\end{cases}$$
The two formulas agree at $p=p_K$. The **star-pressure residual** is
$$\Phi(p)=f_L(p)+f_R(p)+u_R-u_L,\qquad p>0.$$
This is a scalar root equation; it does not itself define a Riemann solution.
def-local-rarefaction-curve:
## Definition

On a neighborhood where an eigenvector field $r_i$ is $C^2$, the local
$i$-rarefaction curve through $u_0$ is the unique local solution
$$\frac{dR_i}{d\sigma}(\sigma;u_0)=r_i(R_i(\sigma;u_0)),\qquad R_i(0;u_0)=u_0.$$
The parameter $\sigma$ is the signed integral-curve parameter for the chosen
normalization of $r_i$. Existence on a common small interval for nearby $u_0$
follows from [[cor-uniform-picard-lindelof-for-nearby-initial-values]]; the
$C^2$ flow on a compact local tube follows from
[[thm-c2-ode-flow-on-common-tube]]. No global integral curve is asserted.
lem-local-characteristic-shock-curve:
## Statement

Let $f$ be $C^3$ and let $\bar u$ have a simple real eigenpair
$(\lambda_i(\bar u),r_i(\bar u))$. There are a neighborhood $N_0$ of $\bar u$,
$\eta>0$, and $C^1$ functions $v_i(\sigma,u_0),s_i(\sigma,u_0)$ for
$u_0\in N_0$, $|\sigma|<\eta$, such that, with $\ell_i(u_0)$ the dual left
eigenvector normalized by $\ell_i(u_0)\cdot r_i(u_0)=1$,
$$\ell_i(u_0)\cdot v_i(\sigma,u_0)=1,\qquad S_i(\sigma;u_0)=u_0+\sigma v_i(\sigma,u_0),$$
and for $\sigma\ne0$ the pair $(u_0,S_i(\sigma;u_0))$ satisfies
Rankine–Hugoniot with speed $s_i(\sigma,u_0)$. Also
$S_i(0;u_0)=u_0$ and $\partial_\sigma S_i(0;u_0)=r_i(u_0)$. If the $i$th
field is genuinely nonlinear on $N_0$ and
$d_i(u):=D\lambda_i(u)r_i(u)$ has constant nonzero sign, then all sufficiently
small nonzero strengths with $\sigma d_i(u_0)<0$ give strict Lax $i$-shocks.
lem-rankine-hugoniot-jump-is-a-weak-solu:
## Statement

For constant states $u_L,u_R$ and a constant speed $s$, the function equal to
$u_L$ on $x<st$ and $u_R$ on $x>st$ solves $u_t+\partial_xf(u)=0$ in
distributions on $t>0$ if and only if
$f(u_R)-f(u_L)=s(u_R-u_L)$.
thm-hll-flux-is-consistent-and-conservat:
## Statement

When $S_L<0<S_R$, the HLL intermediate state
$$u_* =\frac{S_Ru_R-S_Lu_L-(f_R-f_L)}{S_R-S_L}$$
satisfies the Rankine–Hugoniot balance across both waves, and its flux at
$\xi=0$ is the middle formula in [[def-hll-two-wave-flux]]. For equal states
the HLL flux is consistent. A finite-volume update using the same HLL flux at
each periodic interface is conservative: for any finite periodic array with
adjacent pairs in the flux domain, define
$$U_j^{new}=U_j-\nu\bigl(\widehat f_{\rm HLL}(U_j,U_{j+1})-\widehat f_{\rm HLL}(U_{j-1},U_j)\bigr).$$
Here $n\ge1$. The result holds for any scalar $\nu$ and assumes the supplied speeds; it does
not prove that they enclose a nonlinear Riemann fan.
thm-one-dimensional-ideal-gas-euler-eige:
## Statement

For $U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathcal G_\gamma$, put $u=m/\rho$,
$H=(E+p)/\rho$, and $c=\sqrt{\gamma p/\rho}$. The flux Jacobian has the
three simple real eigenvalues and right eigenvectors
$$\lambda_-=u-c,\qquad r_-=(1,u-c,H-uc)^T,$$
$$\lambda_0=u,\qquad r_0=(1,u,u^2/2)^T,$$
$$\lambda_+=u+c,\qquad r_+=(1,u+c,H+uc)^T.$$
The middle field is linearly degenerate; the acoustic fields are genuinely
nonlinear, with $D\lambda_-r_-=-(\gamma+1)c/(2\rho)$ and
$D\lambda_+r_+=(\gamma+1)c/(2\rho)$.
thm-roe-flux-is-consistent-and-conservat:
## Statement

For any supplied Roe matrix, the Roe flux is consistent:
$\widehat f_{\rm Roe}(u,u)=f(u)$. For a finite periodic array define
$$U_j^{new}=U_j-\nu\bigl(\widehat f_{j+1/2}-\widehat f_{j-1/2}\bigr),$$
where $\widehat f_{j+1/2}=\widehat f_{\rm Roe}(U_j,U_{j+1})$ and indices are
modulo $n$, with $n\ge1$. For any scalar $\nu$, the update preserves the sum of cell states. The
Roe jump property is the defining matrix identity in
[[def-roe-linearization-and-flux]] and is not an entropy assertion.
lem-euler-acoustic-wave-pressure-respons:
## Statement

For a side state $K=(\rho_K,u_K,p_K)$ and any trial pressure $p>0$, the
rarefaction/shock branches defined in
[[def-euler-star-pressure-response]] give the magnitude of the velocity change
along the corresponding acoustic wave. For a left 1-wave the star velocity is
$u_*=u_L-f_L(p)$; for a right 3-wave it is $u_*=u_R+f_R(p)$. The star density
on a rarefaction branch is
$$\rho_*(p)=\rho_K(p/p_K)^{1/\gamma},$$
and on a compressive shock branch, with $q=p/p_K>1$ and
$\beta=(\gamma-1)/(\gamma+1)$, it is
$$\rho_*(p)=\rho_K\frac{q+\beta}{\beta q+1}.$$
The shock branches satisfy the strict acoustic Lax inequalities. When the two
pressure responses match at a positive $p$, their star states are joined by a
linearly-degenerate contact at speed $u_*$.
lem-linearly-degenerate-characteristic-c:
## Statement

Let $r_i$ be linearly degenerate on a neighborhood and let $R_i(\sigma;u_0)$
be its local rarefaction curve. Then the states $u_0$ and
$u_1=R_i(\sigma;u_0)$ are joined by a Rankine–Hugoniot jump of speed
$\lambda_i(u_0)$, and the corresponding moving discontinuity is a weak
solution. The characteristic speed is equal on the two sides; this is a
contact wave, not a strict Lax shock.
lem-local-rarefaction-fan:
## Statement

Let $r_i$ be a $C^1$ genuinely nonlinear field on a neighborhood, with
$D\lambda_i(u)r_i(u)$ of constant nonzero sign. If $\sigma\ne0$ satisfies
$\sigma D\lambda_i(u_0)r_i(u_0)>0$ and is sufficiently small, then the
left/right data $u_0,R_i(\sigma;u_0)$ are connected by a centered rarefaction
fan. It is a self-similar weak solution with those Riemann data.
def-mixed-characteristic-wave-curve:
## Definition

Fix a local characteristic family on a neighborhood where it is either
genuinely nonlinear with constant sign $d_i=D\lambda_i\,r_i\ne0$, or linearly
degenerate. For a genuinely nonlinear family define
$$\Psi_i(\sigma;u)=\begin{cases}R_i(\sigma;u),&\sigma d_i>0,\\S_i(\sigma;u),&\sigma d_i<0,\\u,&\sigma=0.\end{cases}$$
where $R_i$ is the local rarefaction curve and $S_i$ the local shock curve of
[[lem-local-characteristic-shock-curve]]. For a linearly degenerate family set
$\Psi_i(\sigma;u)=R_i(\sigma;u)$ for either sign; its nonzero-strength wave is
the contact of [[lem-linearly-degenerate-characteristic-contact]]. The
parameter $\sigma$ is local and is restricted so the entire curve stays in the
chosen neighborhood.
thm-euler-star-pressure-root-and-vacuum-:
## Statement

For the data of [[def-euler-star-pressure-response]], let
$$\Phi(0+):=u_R-u_L-\frac{2(c_L+c_R)}{\gamma-1}.$$
If $\Phi(0+)<0$, then $\Phi$ has exactly one zero $p_*>0$. By the acoustic
wave-response lemma this is the unique positive pressure at which the left and
right wave curves can be joined by a contact. It lies in the
explicit bracket $0<p_*<P$, where, writing
$D=\max\{0,u_L-u_R\}$ and $K=\sqrt{A_L}+\sqrt{A_R}$,
$$P=2\max\{p_L,p_R\}+\frac{6D^2}{K^2}+p_L.$$
If $\Phi(0+)\ge0$, then there is no positive matching pressure. The limiting
left and right rarefaction-tail velocities are ordered with a vacuum gap, or
coincide at the zero-pressure equality threshold. No other vacuum condition is
asserted.
alg-safeguarded-euler-star-pressure-solv:
## Definition

Assume exact-real arithmetic in which each arithmetic operation, comparison,
square root, real power on a positive argument, scalar residual evaluation,
and call to the one-step Newton procedure terminates. **Inputs:**
admissible primitive states $(\rho_L,u_L,p_L)$ and $(\rho_R,u_R,p_R)$, gas
constant $\gamma>1$, pressure-width tolerance $\tau>0$, and iteration budget
$N\in\mathbb N_0$. **Outputs:** `inadmissible-input`, `vacuum`,
`pressure-bracket` with an interval, or `budget-exhausted` with an interval.
The procedure never treats a nonzero residual tolerance as an exact root.

1. If $\rho_L,\rho_R,p_L,p_R$ are not all positive or $\gamma\le1$, return
   `inadmissible-input` before evaluating a wave response.
2. Compute $\Phi(0+)$ from
   [[thm-euler-star-pressure-root-and-vacuum-criterion]]. If $\Phi(0+)\ge0$,
   return `vacuum`.
3. Otherwise set the bracket $[a,b]=[0,P]$ with $P$ from that theorem. Its
   endpoint convention is $\Phi(a):=\Phi(0+)<0<\Phi(b)$.
4. For at most $N$ iterations, in this order:
   1. If $b-a\le\tau$, return `pressure-bracket` with $[a,b]$.
   2. Let $m=(a+b)/2$. Call
      [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on the scalar residual
      $F(p)=\Phi(p)$ over the open domain $(0,\infty)$, starting at $m$, with
      residual tolerance $0$ and update budget $1$.
   3. If Newton returns $(r,\texttt{root})$, return `pressure-bracket` with
      $[r,r]$. If it
      returns `iteration-budget-exhausted` with last iterate $q$ and
      $a+(b-a)/4\le q\le b-(b-a)/4$, use $q$ as the query. In every other
      status or when this central-quarter test fails, use $m$ as the query.
   4. Evaluate $\Phi$ at the query. If it is zero, return `pressure-bracket`
      with the singleton interval. If negative, replace $a$ by the query; if
      positive, replace $b$ by the query.
5. After the budget, return `pressure-bracket` if the width is at most $\tau$;
   otherwise return `budget-exhausted` with the current bracket.

The returned interval uses the zero lower endpoint as a limiting endpoint, not
an admissible pressure. This algorithm gives a finite status and bracket; the
separate theorem below proves its invariant and width reduction. It makes no
claim that an exhausted budget found a root.
lem-mixed-wave-curves-are-c1:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[def-mixed-characteristic-wave-curve]], the map
$(\sigma,u)\mapsto\Psi_i(\sigma;u)$ is $C^1$ near $(0,\bar u)$, with
$\Psi_i(0;u)=u$ and $\partial_\sigma\Psi_i(0;u)=r_i(u)$.
lem-euler-pressure-solver-bracket-and-te:
## Statement

For admissible non-vacuum input data, the algorithm in
[[alg-safeguarded-euler-star-pressure-solver]] terminates after at most $N$
outer iterations and returns either a singleton exact root, a bracket
containing the unique $p_*$ from [[thm-euler-star-pressure-root-and-vacuum-criterion]],
or an explicit budget-exhausted status with that root still bracketed. After
$k$ completed non-exact iterations the bracket width is at most
$(3/4)^kP$. Thus any budget satisfying $(3/4)^N P\le\tau$ returns a
pressure-bracket status. No floating-point or nonlinear convergence guarantee
is asserted.
thm-local-small-data-riemann-solver:
## Statement

Let $f:G\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^3$, let $\bar u\in G$, and suppose on an open
neighborhood $N$ of $\bar u$ the system is strictly hyperbolic and each
characteristic field is either genuinely nonlinear or linearly degenerate. Then
there are $\delta,\eta>0$ such that, whenever
$\|u_L-\bar u\|_2<\delta$ and $\|u_R-\bar u\|_2<\delta$, there is a unique
strength vector $\sigma\in(-\eta,\eta)^m$ satisfying
$$u_R=\Psi_m(\sigma_m;\Psi_{m-1}(\sigma_{m-1};\cdots\Psi_1(\sigma_1;u_L)\cdots)).$$
For the Riemann initial datum $u_0(x)=u_L$ for $x<0$ and $u_R$ for $x>0$,
the corresponding ordered superposition, with waves in increasing family
order, is a self-similar weak solution, meaning it has the form
$u(t,x)=q(x/t)$ for $t>0$. Its nonzero
genuinely nonlinear waves are rarefactions when $\sigma_iD\lambda_i r_i>0$
and strict Lax shocks when $\sigma_iD\lambda_i r_i<0$; its linearly-degenerate
waves are contacts. The neighborhoods are local to $f,N,\bar u$; no arbitrary
large-data solution or uniqueness among all weak solutions is asserted.
def-godunov-flux-from-a-local-riemann-so:
## Definition

For left/right states in the neighborhood of
[[thm-local-small-data-riemann-solver]], let $u(\xi)$ be its self-similar
profile, $\xi=x/t$. The **Godunov flux** is the physical flux through the
interface ray $\xi=0$:
$$G(u_L,u_R)=f(u(0)).$$
If the profile jumps at $\xi=0$, the two traces have the same physical flux by
Rankine–Hugoniot with speed zero, so $G$ is single-valued. This is a local
definition on the data neighborhood where the local solver is established.
thm-godunov-flux-is-consistent-and-conse:
## Statement

For all equal states $u$ in the local solver neighborhood,
$G(u,u)=f(u)$. For any finite periodic array of length $n\ge1$ whose adjacent pairs lie in the
local flux domain, define the update (indices modulo $n$)
$$U_j^{new}=U_j-\nu\bigl(G(U_j,U_{j+1})-G(U_{j-1},U_j)\bigr).$$
For any scalar $\nu$, this update using one two-state flux at each interface
preserves the sum of cell states.
